name: v0.8.0
body:
## New: in-app update check

GhostPiper now tells you when a newer release is available, without you having to check GitHub manually.

- **Update modal** pops once per browser tab on first dashboard load when behind. Shows the version you're on, the latest available, the published date, the full release notes, and the exact command to apply the upgrade.
- **Green "Update Available" pill** in the top nav appears whenever you're behind. Click it to re-open the modal at any time. Stays visible across navigation; no flash.
- **Skip this version** button in the modal silences the auto-pop for that specific version. The list persists on disk (`~/.ghostpiper/cache/skipped_versions.json`). When a newer release lands, the modal pops again.
- **Dismiss** is per-session: the modal goes away until you restart the server or open a new tab.

## New: `ghostpiper --upgrade`

One-shot upgrade. Pulls the latest code, refreshes dependencies, and re-launches the web UI in a single command:

```bash
ghostpiper --upgrade
```

`--upgrade` is a top-level flag, so it works with any subcommand or with none (defaults to launching the web UI after upgrading). Failure-loud: if your working tree is dirty, your branch lacks an upstream, or the target version isn't on your current branch, the upgrade refuses with a clear reason and the literal git command to fix it. No silent half-installs.

## New: Settings -> About sub-page

A new page under Settings collecting version information:

- Current version + git context (branch, `git describe` output, last-commit subject) for any git checkout
- Latest version available on GitHub
- Status with a release-notes panel rendering the full body of the latest release
- Unskip control when you've skipped the current latest and want to bring the modal back
- Last-checked timestamp in human-readable form ("just now", "5 minutes ago", "3 hours ago")
- Links to the GitHub repo and releases page

The page refetches per visit (rate-limited to one network call per minute per server process) so you always see fresh state.

## How the update check works (private-repo background)

Because GhostPiper is a private repo, the GitHub Releases API returns 404 for unauthenticated callers. Update checks therefore poll a small public companion repo (`adam-fff/ghostpiper-releases`) that contains nothing but a single `latest.json` manifest. A new GitHub Action on this repo (`.github/workflows/publish-version.yml`) force-pushes the manifest on every release. Clients hit `raw.githubusercontent.com` directly: no GitHub auth, no per-IP rate limit, fast CDN-cached.

## Configuration

New `[update_check]` section in `ghostpiper.toml`:

```toml
[update_check]
enabled = true                    # Set false to silence the check entirely
interval_hours = 6.0              # Time between background polls
timeout_seconds = 3.0             # HTTP timeout per check
```

Defaults are sane; you don't need to set anything to use the feature.
